security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder URLs, and legitimate Git documentation. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found. The main risk is that the skill teaches and ships workflows for destructive Git operations that require explicit user consent.

remediation.issue: Destructive Git workflows appear in documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Label reset, clean, branch deletion, and force push steps as destructive and require explicit confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: The helper script can change repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Keep confirmation prompts, add a dry-run mode, and show exact branches or files before modifying them.

remediation.issue: SSH troubleshooting references a private key path.
remediation.suggestion: Require user authorization before suggesting ssh-add and prefer explaining key-agent behavior before any command runs.

remediation.issue: Branch cleanup examples use xargs deletion pipelines.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer preview-first loops with validated branch names and include safe handling for empty branch lists.

git branch | grep "feature/your-" | xargs git branch -d

git branch --merged | grep -v "\*\|main\|master\|develop\|development" | xargs -r git branch -d

content.value_statement: Complex Git history, conflicts, and recovery tasks can slow delivery and create data loss risk. This skill provides structured workflows, safety checks, and helper guidance for advanced Git operations.
actual_capabilities: Guides interactive rebases, squashing, splitting, and commit message cleanup.
Explains merge conflict strategies, conflict markers, and ours or theirs choices.
Walks through git bisect workflows for regression isolation.
Covers reflog recovery, lost commits, and history cleanup options.
Provides a shell helper for branch cleanup, conflict assistance, backups, and stash management.
Compares Git Flow, trunk-based, GitHub Flow, and GitLab Flow strategies.
limitations: Does not replace repository backups before destructive Git commands.
Requires user review before force pushes, resets, branch deletion, or history rewrites.
Does not automatically understand team branch policies without project context.
Shell helper actions depend on local Git, shell tools, and repository state.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Clean local commit history, resolve conflicts, and prepare a focused branch for code review.

use_cases.title: Manage Release Branches
use_cases.description: Choose a branch strategy, handle hotfixes, and keep release history understandable.

use_cases.title: Recover From Git Mistakes
use_cases.description: Use reflog, backups, and recovery checks to restore lost commits or undo unsafe changes.

prompt_templates.title: Understand a Conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this merge conflict in plain language. Identify both sides, the likely intent, and the safest resolution steps.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Local Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my recent commit history and propose an interactive rebase plan. Ask before suggesting any destructive operation.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a git bisect workflow for this bug. Include how to choose good and bad commits.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Branch Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Git branch strategy for this team context. Include release, hotfix, and rollback procedures with safety checks.

output_examples.input: I have five messy commits before review.
output_examples.output: A staged cleanup plan that groups related changes, keeps reviewable commits, and asks for confirmation before history rewriting.

output_examples.input: A merge conflict mixes authentication and logging changes.
output: A summary of each side of the conflict.
A test checklist before continuing the merge.

output_examples.input: I accidentally reset my branch and lost work.
output_examples.output: A cautious recovery sequence that checks reflog first, creates a recovery branch, and avoids overwriting remaining work.

best_practices: Create a backup branch before rebases, resets, force pushes, or history rewrites.
Ask for explicit user approval before running repository-changing helper script actions.
Inspect branch state, remotes, and tests before deleting branches or continuing conflict resolution.
anti_patterns: Do not force push shared branches without team coordination and confirmation.
Do not accept all conflict changes from one side without reviewing intent.
Do not run cleanup pipelines on a repository with uncommitted or untracked work.

faq.question: Can this skill run Git commands for me?
faq.answer: It can guide command usage and includes a helper script. Repository-changing commands should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Is it safe for shared branches?
faq.answer: Use extra caution on shared branches. Avoid rebasing or force pushing public history unless your team approves it.

faq.question: Does it support conflict resolution?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains conflict markers, ours and theirs choices, manual merging, and post-resolution checks.

faq.question: Can it recover lost commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers reflog, recovery branches, dangling commits, and safer restoration paths.

faq.question: Does it replace Git expertise?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance, but users must understand repository impact before destructive operations.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
